rules.reaction: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2, dH = -368 kJ/mol (per 2 mol Na)
rules.dT_basis: One of the most violent common alkali-metal/water reactions (routinely ignites the liberated H2) -> pinned near the top of the 0-900K scale at 600K.
rules.note: Already implemented (materials-catalog.json); repeated here for completeness of the chemistry index.

rules.reaction: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO, dH = -1204 kJ/mol O2 (burns at ~3100 C in air)
rules.dT_basis: Adiabatic flame temperature (~3100C) is the hottest common combustion in this set -> ceiling of the range (900K).
rules.note: Already implemented (materials-catalog.json); repeated here for completeness of the chemistry index. 2026-08-26: FIRE-branch needs field changed from O2 to O2=NONE (chem_kinds.lua DSL extension 2, report S4) -- the touching O2 neighbour is now actually consumed (killed) each combustion event, true two-reactant stoichiometry instead of a presence-only gate. The PLSM branch is unchanged (no O2 gate in the original rule).

rules.reaction: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2, dH = -65 kJ/mol
rules.dT_basis: Slaking is strongly exothermic (can flash residual water to steam) but far below a metal-combustion temperature -> mid-high of range (300K).
rules.note: Already implemented (materials-catalog.json); repeated here for completeness of the chemistry index.

rules.reaction: CaC2 + 2H2O -> Ca(OH)2 + C2H2, dH = -125 kJ/mol
rules.dT_basis: Moderately exothermic, well below slaking-lime's per-mol-water release -> low end of range (60K).
rules.note: Already implemented (materials-catalog.json); repeated here for completeness of the chemistry index. 2026-08-26: added :pgas=8 (chem_kinds.lua DSL extension 3, report S4) to the WATR branch alongside the existing extra:GAS particle spawn, so a fresh-water reaction event also adds direct sim.pressure -- a carbide-lamp/acetylene-generator vessel now genuinely pressurizes instead of relying only on individually-spawned GAS particles. Not added to the DSTW branch too: the combined rules string has a hard 64-char live-bridge limit and both branches with pgas would exceed it.

rules.reaction: 2Na + 2H2O -> 2NaOH + H2, dH = -368 kJ/mol (NAK is modeled as ~pure liquid sodium primary coolant)
rules.dT_basis: Identical chemistry to elemental Na, but the coolant is already at 300-350C operating temperature when a breach occurs, matching the historical severity of sodium-cooled-reactor water-ingress fires -> set slightly above NA's baseline at 650K, chance raised to 0.7.

rules.reaction: Breached Na-S cell: Na + H2O -> NaOH + 1/2 H2 (ignites); real NaS grid batteries have documented water-triggered fires
rules.dT_basis: Diluted by co-located sulfur species relative to pure elemental sodium (less free-Na inventory per breach) -> mid-high dT (500K), below NA/NAK's 600-650K.

rules.reaction: 2Al + Fe2O3 -> Al2O3 + 2Fe, dH = -853.5 kJ/mol Al2O3 (thermite; needs a fuse/spark, e.g. burning Mg, to reach ~1500C ignition)
rules.dT_basis: 2026-08-26 rewrite per research-material-mapping-2026-08-26.md S3: this file previously documented BRMT>STNE,IRON:850:.15:FIRE:SMKE while the live materials-catalog.json rule had already drifted to BRMT>STNE,IRON:2500:.8:HEAT400:FIRE (the P13 experiment's setup) -- doc/rule drift, now fixed by replacing both with one live two-stage rule. Stage 1 (FIRE>SELF,SELF:120:.5::FIRE) is a cheap, frequent, non-consuming preheat that warms AL61 and rekindles a forward FIRE without spending the fuel. Stage 2 (BRMT>FSLG,IRON:450:.9:HEAT480:FIRE) only fires once AL61 itself has reached 480K (self-temperature gate via needs=HEAT480, the same mechanism validated in P13), converting AL61 to the new low-HeatConduct FSLG slag (holds heat instead of flash-averaging away per report S0.4) and BRMT to IRON, at a moderate 450K bump and high 0.9 chance chosen so the per-event dT survives the 3x3 conduction-equilibration mechanic. See P14 in experiments-2026-08-26.jsonl for the live test.
rules.caveat: BRMT ('broken metal, formed when iron rusts') stands in for Fe2O3 rust/mill-scale; no dedicated iron-oxide element exists in the catalog. FSLG (new, materials-catalog.json) stands in for real molten Al2O3/Fe slag.

rules.reaction: Ti + O2 -> TiO2, dH = -944 kJ/mol O2 (ignites ~1650C when finely divided/machined; burns white-hot - the well-known 'titanium fire' hazard)
rules.dT_basis: Comparable per-mol exotherm to Mg, but bulk 6Al-4V alloy has a much higher ignition threshold and slower flame spread -> lower dT (700K) and lower chance (.15) than Mg's rule.

rules.reaction: U + O2 -> UO2/U3O8, dH ~ -1085 kJ/mol U (finely divided/adiabatically-sheared DU is pyrophoric, as seen in DU-penetrator post-impact fires)
rules.dT_basis: Real pyrophoricity is a fine-particle/shear-surface phenomenon much less vigorous in bulk armor form than Mg or thermite -> lower-mid dT (500K), low chance (.1) reflecting the need for surface disruption to ignite.

rules.reaction: 2H2O2 -> 2H2O + O2, dH = -98.2 kJ/mol (catalytic decomposition; real catalysts are MnO2, Pt, Ag, or catalase)
rules.dT_basis: Decomposition exotherm is moderate (drives high-test-peroxide monopropellant thrusters hot, but not combustion-hot) -> mid-low of range (250K).
rules.caveat: No MnO2/Pt/catalase element exists in the catalog. MG was chosen over MERC as the catalyst proxy because mercury is not a real peroxide-decomposition catalyst, whereas Mg (already reactive-metal-flavoured) is the nearest available analog; MG is left unchanged (OTHER_BECOMES=SELF) to approximate catalytic (non-consumed) behavior. 2026-08-26: added :conc=20 (chem_kinds.lua DSL extension 1, report S4) so the peroxide only fully converts to WTRV after ~5 MG contacts (life 100 -> 0 at -20/hit) instead of vanishing on the first hit -- a gradual concentration-depletion decomposition instead of a one-shot conversion. Also fixed the invalid explosive=15 flag (S0.3/S1.4) to 0, since the pressure-autodetonation bit was never an intended behavior and this decomposition rule already carries the peroxide's real hazard.
rules.explosive_fix: explosive 15 -> 0 (report S0.3: 15 has both native Explosive bits set; bit0 was dead since Flammable was never set, bit1 meant 'detonates whenever local pressure exceeds 2.5' which was not the intent).

rules.reaction: C2H5OH + 3O2 -> 2CO2 + 3H2O, dH = -1367 kJ/mol
rules.dT_basis: Standard alcohol combustion exotherm, mid-high of range (500K); high chance (.4) reflects ethanol's very low flash point (13C) and fast, clean flame spread.

rules.reaction: C12H26 + 18.5O2 -> 12CO2 + 13H2O, dH ~ -7513 kJ/mol (dodecane, representative kerosene component)
rules.dT_basis: Slightly hotter flame than ethanol (denser hydrocarbon fuel) but a higher flash point (~50C) makes it harder to sustain-ignite -> 550K, lower chance (.3).

rules.reaction: FAME (e.g. methyl oleate) + O2 -> CO2 + H2O, combustion enthalpy on the order of ~38 MJ/kg, similar to petrodiesel
rules.dT_basis: Same combustion-exotherm tier as kerosene, but biodiesel's notably higher flash point (130-170C) makes it much harder to ignite -> same dT (500K) but a low chance (.15).
Sizeable combustion enthalpy on paper, but glycerol's viscosity and very low vapor pressure make it burn reluctantly -> mild dT (350K) and very low chance (.05).

rules.reaction: CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O + CO2, dH = -17 kJ/mol (classic acid-carbonate fizz test)
rules.dT_basis: Only mildly exothermic -> low end of range (80K); chance reflects limestone's modest porosity/reactivity.

rules.reaction: CaCO3 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O + CO2, dH = -17 kJ/mol (same carbonate chemistry as limestone)
rules.dT_basis: Same mild exotherm as limestone; chance roughly doubled (0.3 vs 0.15) to reflect marble's documented higher vulnerability to acid attack (the real basis of acid-rain erosion of marble statuary).

rules.reaction: 2Cu + O2 + CO2 + H2O -> Cu2CO3(OH)2 (basic copper carbonate patina, e.g. Statue of Liberty verdigris)
rules.dT_basis: Patina formation is a very slow, only mildly exothermic surface oxidation -> near-zero dT (2K); chance pinned to the slow-corrosion floor (0.001), a multi-year real-world timescale.
rules.caveat: BRMT ('broken/corroded metal') is used as the only available corroded-metal proxy even though real patina is green verdigris, not rust-brown; chemistry direction (slow oxidative corrosion) is correct.

rules.reaction: Cu-Zn brass tarnishes via slow surface oxidation/dezincification
rules.dT_basis: Slower than pure copper because the zinc component contributes its own passivating oxide -> half CU's chance (0.0005).

rules.reaction: Cu-Sn bronze forms a protective, extremely slow patina
rules.dT_basis: Bronze is prized specifically for outlasting brass/copper in corrosion resistance -> lowest chance of the three copper alloys (0.0003).

rules.reaction: 4Fe + 3O2 + 2H2O -> 2Fe2O3.H2O (rust), dH ~ -824 kJ/mol Fe2O3 overall
rules.dT_basis: Ordinary steel rusting is slow and only mildly exothermic per particle -> near-floor dT (3K); chance (0.004) sits in the slow-corrosion band, matching the catalog description's explicit call-out that rebar 'rusts easily / low corrosion resistance'.

rules.reaction: Same rusting chemistry as RBAR (4Fe + 3O2 + 2H2O -> 2Fe2O3.H2O)
rules.dT_basis: Same basis as RBAR; chance trimmed slightly (0.003 vs 0.004) to reflect cast iron's coarser microstructure corroding a touch slower than bare mild-steel bar stock in practice.

rules.reaction: Lignin combustion, same order-of-magnitude enthalpy as cellulose (~17 MJ/kg)
rules.dT_basis: 2026-08-26 bugfix per report S2: this rule was previously byte-identical to CELL's (FIRE>NONE,SELF:300:.2:O2:SMKE) despite LIGN's own description claiming it 'chars rather than flaming as readily as pure cellulose, harder to ignite' -- no numeric differentiation existed. Chance lowered 0.2 -> 0.12 (dT left at 300, same combustion-family tier as CELL/SUGR) so the description is now actually true in-sim.

rules.reaction: 2Cs + 2H2O -> 2CsOH + H2, dH per-kg lower than K's despite Cs being the more kinetically dramatic alkali metal
rules.dT_basis: 2026-08-26 rebalance per report S2: dT lowered 900 -> 400, now below K's 800, fixing an ordering inversion (Cs has *lower* per-kg reaction energy than K -- heavier atom, similar molar dH -- yet previously had a *higher* dT). The 'most dramatic alkali metal' framing now lives entirely in `chance` (0.9, already above K's 0.6-0.7) rather than an inflated dT.

stock_proposals.reaction: Rusting: 4Fe + 3O2 + 2H2O -> 2Fe2O3.H2O, dH ~ -824 kJ/mol Fe2O3. Acid attack: Fe + 2HCl -> FeCl2 + H2, dH ~ -88 kJ/mol Fe
stock_proposals.dT_basis: Rusting is the classic slow, near-zero-exotherm corrosion (3K, 0.002 chance = a 'takes years' rate), independent of stock IRON's existing salt-triggered corrosion. Acid dissolution is a visibly faster, more vigorous reaction that fizzes H2 -> higher dT (60K) and chance (0.15), but still well short of a violent alkali-metal reaction.
stock_proposals.note: Stock IRON's description ('Rusts with salt, can be used for electrolysis of WATR') implies a salt/electrolysis-specific native path already exists; this proposal adds the independent plain-water-plus-air rusting path and a distinct acid-attack path with H2 evolution, matching the reaction pattern given in the task brief.
